title: Kinematics
summary: Wheel speeds to robot speeds, the WPILib way.

steps.title: The job: wheel speeds in, robot speeds out

say.never:
Last lesson you worked out the robot's speed with your own math. WPILib, the robot toolkit, has a class that does it for you: `DifferentialDriveKinematics`. You give it the two wheel speeds, and it gives back the robot's forward speed and turning speed together in a single object called `ChassisSpeeds`.

Say the left side does 3.0 m/s and the right side does 5.0 m/s. Kinematics works out that the robot moves forward at 4.0 m/s (the average) and turns at (5.0 - 3.0) / track width radians per second.

You will open `DifferentialDriveMech.java`, fill in `getChassisSpeeds()`, then compare your robot's speed with your own math from last lesson in AdvantageScope.
say.bit: `DifferentialDriveKinematics` does the math you wrote by hand last lesson: wheel speeds in, a `ChassisSpeeds` (forward and turning) out.

say.never:
`getChassisSpeeds()` takes two moves. First **bundle** the two wheel speeds into one `DifferentialDriveWheelSpeeds` object, built from `getLeftMetersPerSecond()` and `getRightMetersPerSecond()`. Then **convert**: hand that bundle to `kinematics_` with `toChassisSpeeds`, and return what comes back.

The answer has `vxMetersPerSecond` (forward) and `omegaRadiansPerSecond` (turning). A method can only return once, so replace the placeholder return instead of adding a second one.
say.bit: Bundle the two speeds as `DifferentialDriveWheelSpeeds`, then `kinematics_.toChassisSpeeds(...)` gives forward and turning.

say.never:

Click **I did it** when both are written.
